questions.title: Which DRC province will WHO identify as experiencing a surge in weekly Ebola cases in mid-September 2026?
questions.background: The Democratic Republic of Congo declared an Ebola outbreak in May 2026.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : WHO public statements about the DRC Ebola outbreak, including statements quoted in contemporaneous reputable news reporting. Resolution Window : Resolve to the province explicitly identified by WHO as experiencing surging weekly Ebola cases in its outbreak assessment publicly reported between September 10 and September 16, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the province.
questions.current_reasoning: WHO DON612 (July 3, data through July 1) and WHO's July 4 sitrep (reported July 6 by Al Jazeera) show DRC Bundibugyo Ebola accelerating to 1,561 confirmed cases and 506 deaths (+665 cases since June 19) with no approved vaccine. Ituri still accounts for 91.3% of confirmed cases (1,333/1,460), expanded to 3 additional health zones (24/36 HZs), nearly doubled active contacts to 8,376, entered Bunia's 15,000-person Kigonze IDP camp, saw a health facility burned on June 30, and faces a July 6 front-line health-worker strike—lifting Ituri to 0.39. North Kivu trims from 0.35 to 0.28 after stalling at 11/35 affected health zones over June 19-July 1 (with M23 authorities claiming eradication in controlled zones), though 2,445 active contacts and a worrying 57.4% mortality rate keep it clear #2. South Kivu drops sharply (0.14 -> 0.06) after WHO confirmed zero new cases since May 26 and all previously listed contacts completed 21-day follow-up. Conversely, cross-province spillover just hit Tshopo (a deceased Ebola patient's body was transported 300 km by motorcycle from Ituri into Kisangani, a city of 1.5M) and Haut-Uele (fleeing Ituri contacts diagnosed in Wamba HZ with a death reported), raising Tshopo to 0.13 and Haut-Uele to 0.10, with 4% left for Kinshasa (107 contacts of the French doctor) and other provinces.

questions.title: In which country outside Iran, if any, will US forces strike Iran-aligned armed groups between July 22 and July 29, 2026?
questions.background: Iran-aligned armed groups operate across several Middle Eastern countries, creating potential flashpoints for military confrontation with the United States.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Contemporaneous reporting by Al Jazeera, supported where available by official military statements. Resolution Conditions : Identify the country outside Iran where US forces conduct strikes against Iran-aligned armed groups between July 22 and July 29, 2026, inclusive. Direct US participation in either unilateral or joint strikes qualifies; threats, proposed operations, and diplomatic support do not. Accepted Answer Format : The country's name, or “None” if no qualifying strikes occur.
questions.current_reasoning: The July 22-29, 2026 window falls squarely inside the 60-day US-Iran Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding ceasefire (effective June 18 through mid-August), making 'None' the single most likely outcome for a narrow eight-day window if diplomatic talks in Switzerland hold. However, the truce is fragile amid disputes over Hormuz tolls and ongoing Israeli strikes in Lebanon, and during March-April 2026 Iran-backed Iraqi PMF militias (including Kataib Hezbollah) launched ~300 attacks on US sites in Iraq, drawing ~70 US/allied retaliatory strikes—making Iraq by far the primary flashpoint if hostilities flare. Yemen is secondary (the Houthis largely avoided provoking a repeat of Operation Rough Rider during the 2026 war, though Red Sea risks persist), while Iran-backed militia presence in post-Assad Syria is greatly reduced and Lebanon strikes are overwhelmingly conducted by Israel rather than US forces.

local_articles.snippet: Najaf: Thousands of mourners attended funeral processions for Iran's Ayatollah Ali Khamenei on Wednesday in the holy Iraqi cities of Najaf and Karbala as part of dayslong funeral ceremonies for the Islamic Republic's late supreme leader. At some moments, the scene turned chaotic, with mourners swarming the coffin, forcing pallbearers to lower it to avoid losing control. questions.title: Which country will agree to a joint project with Iran to clear sea mines from the Strait of Hormuz by August 26, 2026?
questions.background: Sea mines have been reported near the Strait of Hormuz, a major route for international oil and gas shipments.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the country that agrees with Iran to a joint mine-clearance project in the Strait of Hormuz, as announced in a statement from the two governments by August 26, 2026. Resolution Date : 2026-08-26 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the country's common English name.
questions.current_reasoning: July 4-5 reporting (Al Jazeera, Straits Times/Bloomberg, Khaleej Times) from the World Peace Forum in Beijing meaningfully strengthens Oman's lead as Iran's most likely bilateral partner on Strait of Hormuz clearance/management. Speaking July 4—five days after Oman's Sultan Haitham met Macron in Paris—Iranian Ambassador to China Abdolreza Rahmani Fazli explicitly reaffirmed that Iran is working in 'collaboration and cooperation' with Oman on 'new arrangements' for 'guaranteeing the security of passage' through the strait, and Al Jazeera confirmed Iran and Oman have established a formal joint committee to manage the waterway (even as at least eight ships turned back along the Omani coast July 3-4). This resolves our July 1 concern that Tehran's anti-France demining rebuke (reiterated July 1 by Africanews) had sidelined Oman. Conversely, Bloomberg noted that China—though promised 'special considerations' on future transit fees—has kept to the sidelines of the conflict, merely calling July 3 for unhindered shipping and relying diplomatically on Pakistan. We raise Oman (0.26 -> 0.32) while trimming China (0.25 -> 0.23), Pakistan (0.18 -> 0.17), and Russia (0.14 -> 0.12), keeping Japan at 0.03 (sum 0.87, leaving 13% tail for Qatar, India, Turkey, UAE, etc.).

questions.title: Which European country will announce plans to shut down its only nuclear power plant because of drought-related cooling-water shortages by August 2, 2026?
questions.background: Nuclear power plants that use river water for cooling can face operational restrictions when drought reduces the available water supply.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official government statements or contemporaneous reporting by established news organizations. Resolution Rule : Identify the European country whose government announces, between July 1 and August 2, 2026, inclusive, plans for a complete shutdown of its sole operating nuclear power plant because drought has reduced the river water available for reactor cooling. The announcement of the shutdown plan is sufficient; the shutdown itself need not have occurred. A partial reduction in electricity output alone does not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The country's commonly used English name.
questions.current_reasoning: Only a tiny set of European countries have a sole operating nuclear power plant cooled by river water: Slovenia (Krško, 1 reactor, Sava River), Hungary (Paks, 4 reactors, Danube), Romania (Cernavodă, 2 reactors, Danube), Bulgaria (Kozloduy, 2 reactors, Danube), and Belarus (Astravets, cooling towers, Neris). Slovenia is the clear favorite because Krško already curtailed output in May 2026 due to low Sava River levels before the June Omega heatwave, has only a single reactor (so one shutdown is a complete shutdown), and faces strict 28C thermal limits amid thin Alpine snowpack. Hungary (severe 2026 drought with Lake Velence near 2022 lows; direct once-through Danube cooling) and Romania (Cernavodă fully shut down in the Aug 2003 Danube drought) follow ahead of Bulgaria and Belarus.

questions.title: Which European country will announce a complete drought-related shutdown of its nuclear power generation between August 1 and August 13, 2026?
questions.background: Nuclear reactors require reliable cooling-water supplies. Low river levels can force reactors to shut down, potentially disrupting national electricity supplies.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official announcements by national nuclear operators or governments, corroborated by reliable news reporting. Resolution Conditions : Identify the European country that announces, between August 1 and August 13, 2026, a shutdown covering its entire operating nuclear fleet because drought has left insufficient river water for cooling. An announcement initiating the shutdown of the last operating reactor qualifies; a partial shutdown alone does not. Accepted Answer Format : The country's common English name.
questions.current_reasoning: Unlike the late-July single-plant question, this August 1–13 window covers any European country shutting down its entire operating nuclear fleet ('last operating reactor') due to river drought. Slovenia remains the top candidate (either as a direct follow-through initiating Krško's actual shutdown on the low Sava River or independently). Switzerland jumps into second because June 2026 ETH/SLF reports confirm record-low water levels in the Aare and Rhine rivers and Alpine snowpack at half of normal—directly threatening its small 3-plant river-dependent fleet (Beznau shut down in July 2025 heat)—followed by Danube-cooled single-plant fleets in Hungary, Romania (2003 full-shutdown precedent), and Bulgaria.

questions.title: Which club will sign Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig in summer 2026?
questions.background: Yan Diomande is an Ivory Coast winger playing for RB Leipzig.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official announcement by RB Leipzig or the destination club confirming an agreement for Diomande's permanent transfer. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the destination club in the first such agreement announced between June 1 and August 31, 2026. Loan agreements do not count. Accepted Answer Format : The commonly used name of the destination club.
questions.current_reasoning: Major June 29 Tier-1 breakthrough from BBC Sport (Nizaar Kinsella and Aadam Patel): Yan Diomande would prefer to join Paris Saint-Germain over Liverpool, and PSG—led by Nasser Al-Khelaifi, Luis Campos, and Luis Enrique after back-to-back Champions League titles—are actively aiming to agree a deal with RB Leipzig in the coming weeks. Liverpool previously had an opening bid of £69m plus £17m add-ons (£86m) rejected, and Leipzig are expected to demand around £129m under no financial pressure to sell. Conditional on a summer 2026 permanent transfer, PSG leapfrog Liverpool to 0.60 (from 0.14), while Liverpool drop from 0.68 to 0.28 (retaining a real chance if PSG balk at Leipzig's ~£129m valuation), with small tails for Chelsea (0.04), Real Madrid (0.03), Bayern Munich (0.02), and the field (0.03).
